description: Provider timestamp to a WebSocket message in a real browser page.

environment.note: Single developer machine; PostgreSQL, Redis and a one-broker Kafka in Docker Desktop on the same host as the code under test, sharing its CPU and disk.

workload.feed: synthetic provider at its configured live rate (TW_PROVIDER=synthetic)

configuration.path: producer -> Kafka -> broadcaster -> Redis Pub/Sub -> API /ws/market -> Chrome
configuration.processes: one of each, started by scripts/dev.ps1

does_not_prove: Local loopback networking only: no internet, no load balancer, no TLS. Any real deployment adds those hops.
One browser client. Fan-out cost with many connected clients is not measured.
The synthetic provider's rate is modest; this is latency at light load, not latency under the ingest benchmark's saturation rate.
`next_frame` is the earliest paint opportunity, not a measured paint: React's render of the chart is not included.
